title: Completed pullback preserves shifts and distinguished triangles
statement: Let $u:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes. Fix the Noetherian adic datum $(A,I)$ of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], including finite perfect quotients $P_n=A/I^n$ for $n\geq1$, and use its completed ring sheaves $A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$ on the small pro-etale sites, for $W=T,T'$. Let $P_u=Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ be precisely the strict-tower completed pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], defined on the full subcategory of derived $I$-complete objects of $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))$ [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. It has natural shift isomorphisms $P_u(M[r])\cong P_u(M)[r]$ for $r\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying the shift unit and composition identities. For every ambient distinguished triangle $M\to N\to Q\to M[1]$ whose three vertices are derived $I$-complete, the image triangle, with final arrow followed by this shift comparison, is distinguished in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_{T'}))$ [def-weil-triangulated-category]. This assertion concerns the specified reduction-tower, derived tower pullback and derived inverse limit construction; it assumes no constructibility or noetherianity of the schemes.

proof.text: Write $R(K)=K_\bullet$ for the reduction-tower functor. In the adic-datum definition its underived functor on complexes is $F(P)_n=P\otimes_{A_T}(P_n)_T$, with the quotient transitions. The definition states that $F$ preserves shifts and cone complexes and that K-flat resolutions exist and carry quasi-isomorphisms between resolving objects to tower quasi-isomorphisms. Apply the resolving-class theorem to this exact functor from the homotopy category, with K-flat complexes as the resolving class. Its conclusion says that the left derived functor $R:D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_T))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T))$ is exact. Thus the given ambient distinguished triangle is sent to a distinguished triangle of strict towers, with its connecting arrow followed by the shift comparison of $R$.

source.place: Tags 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual part, and 05SE (proposition-derived-functor); reduction functor as specified in def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum

proof.text: Use the coefficient map $c_u:u^{-1}A_T\to A_{T'}$ in the completed-pullback definition. The underived tower pullback $H$ applies $u^{-1}(-)\otimes_{u^{-1}A_T}A_{T'}$ levelwise. It is additive, so on complexes it respects the shift signs and the cone differential matrix: $H(\operatorname{Cone}(a))^q=H(Q^q)\oplus H(P^{q+1})$ for $a:P\to Q$, and its differential has entries $H(d_Q),H(a),-H(d_P)$. It therefore induces an exact functor from the tower homotopy category to the target tower derived category. Apply the strict-diagram K-flat replacement lemma with the small category $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}}$, the two small pro-etale sites, their completed ring sheaves and $c_u$. It supplies replacements for every tower complex and quasi-isomorphism invariance of $H$ on that resolving class. These are exactly the two hypotheses of the resolving-class theorem. Consequently its total left derived functor $V=Lu^*_{\operatorname{Tow}}$ is exact. This is the tower functor used in the completed-pullback definition. In particular it takes the triangle of Step 1 to a distinguished triangle in $D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T'))$. No exactness of underived completed-ring pullback is assumed.

source.place: Tags 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), dual part, and 05SE (proposition-derived-functor), applied to the strict-diagram resolving class

proof.text: The derived inverse-limit proposition gives an exact functor $L=\operatorname{Rlim}:D(\operatorname{Tow}_A(T'))\to D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_{T'}))$. Apply it to the distinguished triangle of Step 2. By the completed-pullback definition, its three vertices are precisely $P_u(M),P_u(N),P_u(Q)$, since $P_u=LVR$ on derived-complete inputs. Its last arrow is $LVR$ applied to the original connecting morphism, followed successively by the images of the shift comparisons for $R$, $V$, and $L$. Thus it has the required connecting arrow for the composite shift comparison. This argument uses the strict-tower derived functor of inverse limit, not a choice of unrelated homotopy-limit cones.

proof.text: First, the complete-object domain is stable under shifts: the tensor, product and mapping-fiber formulas in the intrinsic-completion definition commute with shifting complexes (with the usual differential signs), and identify the completion unit for $K[r]$ with $\eta_K[r]$. Thus an invertible $\eta_K$ remains invertible after any shift. For an exact functor, its natural comparison with $[1]$ extends to all integer shifts by iteration, using the inverse comparison for $[-1]$ and the identity for $[0]$. For positive shifts the two sides of the addition identity are the same ordered string of comparisons; for negative shifts they are strings of inverses; in mixed signs the inverse adjacent factors cancel. This gives the unit and addition identities, with the usual shift associativity identifications. Let $\sigma_R^r,\sigma_V^r,\sigma_L^r$ be these comparisons for the three exact functors. Define the comparison for their composite by the explicit composite $LVR(K[r])\xrightarrow{LV(\sigma_R^r)}LV(RK[r])\xrightarrow{L(\sigma_V^r)}L(VRK[r])\xrightarrow{\sigma_L^r}LVRK[r]$. Naturality follows by composing the three naturality squares. For $r=0$ every factor is an identity. For $r+s$, substitute each factor's addition identity into this formula; naturality moves the inner comparisons past the outer ones, producing first the displayed comparison for $r$ and then its shifted comparison for $s$. This is the required composition identity. Restricting this natural comparison to the full complete-object domain gives the claimed shifts for $P_u$; Step 3 proves distinguishedness for the same comparison at $r=1$. No scheme finiteness or constructibility assumption was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q05-ad2ad70aa (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item in full and every cited statement: adic datum, completed pullback, intrinsic completion, def-weil-triangulated-category, lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements, prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality, plus the main-20261015 blueprint_updates. I also read the Stacks sources 06XN, 05SE, 014V, 0941 and 099N(2),(5) at the cited places. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. It uses the completed coefficient sheaves A_W on both sides with the structure map c_u, and does not identify them with constant coefficients. Step 1: the adic-datum definition supplies both resolving-class hypotheses (K-flat resolutions exist; quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes go to tower quasi-isomorphisms), so the derived reduction R is exact. Step 2: the diagram lemma's two clauses apply with small J=N_{>=1}^op, small pro-etale sites, commutative A_T and A_{T'}, and the ring map c_u. Its objectwise quasi-isomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms of towers because tower cohomology is levelwise. Additivity gives exactness on the homotopy category, so V=Lu*_Tow is exact, and V is literally the functor of the definition. Step 3: prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality gives Rlim triangulated with no boundedness hypothesis, and P_u=Rlim.V.R by definition. Step 4: the domain is stable under shifts and the composite shift comparison is written out explicitly; this is honestly elementary. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and there is no cycle. Small cases (I=A, I=0, split triangles, A=Z_l with I=(l)) are consistent. I accept the tool_uses for the three off-unit generic tools lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class, lem-weil-pbc-diagram-kflat-replacements and prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality; the three definitions listed there are notions and need none. The delivery creates no new nodes. rg over dag/nodes found no duplicate: lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange is O_E-only and asserts linearity and adjunction, not triangle preservation. The parent thm-cbc-finite-extension uses exactly this conclusion. No SGA source is used. No changes.

lean.statement: theorem completedPullback_preserves_shifts_distinguished (g : X ⟶ Y) (d : AdicCoefficientDatum A) : ∃ h : (pbcActualCompletedPull g d).CommShift ℤ, (fun [shift : (pbcActualCompletedPull g d).CommShift ℤ] ↦ ∀ (T : Triangle (PbcCompletedDerived Y d)), T ∈ distTriang _ → PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete Y d T.obj₁ → PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete Y d T.obj₂ → PbcIsIntrinsicallyComplete Y d T.obj₃ → (pbcActualCompletedPull g d).mapTriangle.obj T ∈ distTriang _) (shift := h)
